summary: Umpqua NF summit lookout: built 1911 or 1914-15 (sources disagree), L-4 cab 1938, burned or removed 1965; a concrete foundation is reported on the summit in 2024.

facts.design: Glass-walled station on a concrete base (1914-15); cupola and new roof 1926; L-4 cab built in 1938 on the old lower walls
facts.status_note: The cab was burned or removed in 1965; the concrete foundation is reported still on the summit (2007 and 2024 accounts)

visit.trail_note: A 2024 hiker's blog describes a 2.6-mile drive up Road 950 to Whitehorse Meadows Trailhead, then a route through a 2009 burn to an old trail. This is a personal account, not an agency statement

events.note: First fire lookout on the Umpqua: an observation point with a compass
Register says the cab was built in 1911. Forest Lookouts describes an alidade on a pole platform in use by about 1911. The 1914-15 accounts conflict; see resolved_conflicts
Glass-walled house with stone and concrete walls, described as built on the summit in February 1915; being pushed to completion in September 1914
J. H. Bosard assigned as the forestry lookout
Minerva Bidwell served at the lookout for the 1919 season (reported in 1920)
Cupola and new roof added to the lookout house
Ernest Taylor stationed at the lookout for the summer
L-4 cab built atop the existing lower walls, replacing the cupola house
Staffed for 80 days; reported to the Big Camas Ranger Station by forest telephone line
September 1942 'Report on Lookout and Guard Stations': 65-mile road trip from Roseburg, then an 8-mile trail to the summit
Forest Service burned the discontinued lookout building. Register says removed in 1965; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1965
June 2007: foundation has survived; Forest Lookouts calls it a monument to possibly the oldest lookout site in Oregon
Hiker's blog post dated June 21, 2024 reports the old foundation still on the summit; the visit date itself is not given

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the cab to 1911, but 1914-15 newspaper accounts describe a glass-walled house being built on the summit. The sources do not reconcile these; the story gives both dates and attributes each.

The register says the cab was removed in 1965, firelookout.com says destroyed, and Forest Lookouts says the Forest Service burned the discontinued building. The story attributes the burning to Forest Lookouts and mentions the other two accounts.

notes_for_editor: Location conflict is unresolved and the story gives no coordinates: the current record uses the FFLA point 43.16, -122.464, while the FFLOS register gives 43.19564, -122.2922, about 14 km apart. Both name Umpqua NF and Douglas County. Check against the forest map before using either point. Forest Lookouts gives the forest location as 28S-3E-4 (not checked against a map). Build date and fate conflicts are reported, not resolved. The 2024 account is a personal blog, so access today is unconfirmed and the story says so. No access level is recorded because no agency source describes current access. Staffing as_of 1965 is inferred from the building being described as discontinued.
